claims.title: Doc comment says non-P0 but code only drops P2/P3
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Doc comment says non-P0 but code only drops P2/P3**

The comment says the option drops "non-P0 findings". `droppedFamilies` returns `[]` for anything other than P2 or P3, so P1 findings are never dropped. The PR's own tests ("never drops a P1 either") and CLAUDE.md both say this. A maintainer reading the option doc would wrongly conclude P1 findings are eligible. The note that it "runs before every other merge step" is also looser than the code. Resolved-key filtering and dedup come after it, but the per-agent event downgrade happens inside it.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
	/** Drop P2/P3 findings (never P0, P1 or suppressible:false) whose own title
	 * or closing sentence says there is no defect. Runs before every other merge step. */
```

claims.title: Hard-coded "all 15 filler claims" in the margin report
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Hard-coded "all 15 filler claims" in the margin report**

`formatMargin` always prints "phrases were designed after reading all 15 filler claims", whatever fixtures and class files are passed in. The command test seeds a fixture with zero filler claims and the line still says 15. If the class files or fixtures are regenerated, or the report is run on a different corpus, the line becomes a false statement. Interpolate `m.total.filler.of`, or word it without a number.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
		`  recall is resubstitution: phrases were designed after reading all ${t.filler.of} filler claims`,
```

claims.title: Closing "no issues found in <scope>" can drop a finding that states a real defect earlier
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Closing "no issues found in <scope>" can drop a finding that states a real defect earlier**

`no-actionable-defect` only inspects the last sentence of the body. It tolerates up to 4 words after the phrase, so a scoped closer such as "No issues found in the happy path." or "No issues found in tests." matches. Neither contains a contrast word, an exception word or a request, so the finding is dropped even when the earlier sentences describe a concrete defect. Example: "The retry loop drops the token on 429. No issues found in the happy path." as a P2/P3 finding. The negative tests only cover scopes of 6 or more words ("in the rest of the file"), so the 4-word boundary is the exact edge that leaks. Drops are only logged and are not surfaced in the review, so a lost real finding is invisible to the author. Consider requiring that the phrase is not followed by a locative qualifier (`in`/`on`/`for`/`within` ...). Alternatively, only apply this family when the earlier sentences are short or are themselves non-defect statements. Add negative tests for "in the happy path" and "in tests".

claims.title: Four-word scope tail after "No issues found" lets real findings be dropped
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Four-word scope tail after "No issues found" lets real findings be dropped**

The `no-actionable-defect` family only keeps a finding when more than `NO_ACTIONABLE_AFTER_WORDS` (4) words follow the phrase. A real P2/P3 finding whose last sentence adds a short scope qualifier is therefore treated as a retraction. For example: "The migration deletes rows without a backup. No issues found in this file." Here ` in this file` is 3 words, so `isSelfRetracted` returns true and the finding is silently dropped from the merged review. The same happens with `Logs say 'No issues found' even when the scan fails`, because only backtick spans are stripped, not quotes. The existing negative tests only cover tails of 5 or more words ("in the rest of the file"). The 4-word cutoff is fitted to those examples, and there is no test just below it. Consider requiring the phrase to end the sentence, or allowing only a small whitelist of tails such as `here`, `this round`, `in this file`, and add negative tests for 1 to 4-word tails that follow a real defect sentence. The drops are logged and limited to P2/P3, so impact is bounded, but a dropped finding never reaches the author.

claims.title: Doc comment still gives "looks resolved by ..." as a retraction example
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Doc comment still gives "looks resolved by ..." as a retraction example**

This doc comment still lists "this looks resolved by ..." as a retracted phrase. After this change that shape is kept: "by" is in `SCOPE_FOLLOWS`, which now applies to every family whenever the phrase doesn't open the whole finding. The test that used "This looks resolved by the explicit `kubectl rollout restart` call." as a positive was rewritten to bare "This looks resolved." for the same reason. Update the example so it matches the current behavior, e.g. "this looks resolved" with no trailing scope or with-clause.

claims.title: Whole-title no-new-findings pattern swallows trailing contrast or exception text
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Whole-title no-new-findings pattern swallows trailing contrast or exception text**

The first alternative now ends with `(?:\s+beyond (?:the )?(?:prior|previous|earlier)\b[^.]*)?\W*$`. The greedy `[^.]*` consumes everything after `beyond the prior`, up to a period or the end of the text. A closer like `No new findings beyond the prior reviews, except the missing timeout` or `..., but the retry path leaks` therefore matches in full, and `rest` after the match is empty. That means `EXCEPTION_FOLLOWS`, `SCOPE_FOLLOWS` and any keep-rule that reads `rest` never see the exception or contrast clause. If those keep-rules do read `rest`, the finding is retracted anyway. The new 'applies exception words to every family' test only covers `apart from`, `other than` and `except` with no `beyond ... prior` prefix, so it misses this path. Restrict the tail so it cannot absorb contrast or exception words, for example by capping it at a few words with `[^.,;]*` or by rejecting the `CONTRAST` and `EXCEPTION_FOLLOWS` words inside it. Add a negative test for `No new findings beyond the prior reviews, except X`.

claims.title: Comma-led scope words now keep plain closers like "No issues found, as expected"
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Comma-led scope words now keep plain closers like "No issues found, as expected"**

`SCOPE_FOLLOWS` now starts with `^[\s,]*`, so a scope word after a comma counts as scoping the phrase. Words like `as`, `per`, `if`, `when` and `after` are common retraction tails, not scopes.

Take a multi-sentence finding whose last sentence is `No issues found, as expected.` The phrase doesn't open the whole finding, and `, as` now matches `SCOPE_FOLLOWS`, so the finding is kept. Before this change it was dropped. The same applies to `No actionable defect, per the earlier review.`

The `ai-listings` fixture claim `r3:c4371932215:1` stopped being dropped in this same change (recall fell from 13 to 12). The PR attributes that drop to the quote and consistent/resolved fixes, but I can't tell from the diff which rule caused it. Only the 12-of-15 numbers changed. There is no test that pins comma-led scope words either way, so the behaviour change is unpinned.

Consider limiting the comma allowance to the exception regex only, and pinning intended comma-scope cases with tests.

claims.title: Fix-wording check also matches negated statements
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Fix-wording check also matches negated statements**

`FIX_WORDING` matches any sentence containing "fixed", "resolved", "addressed" and similar words, without checking for negation. A reply such as "This was not fixed in abcdef1; the behavior is intended" or "Not addressed in abcdef1 on purpose" still classifies the claim as `stale`, even though it is contradicted evidence. The new test only covers replies with no fix word at all. Either skip sentences where a negator (not, never, wasn't, isn't) precedes the fix word, or add a negative test and accept the limitation.

The detector now lives in src/replay/retraction-rule.ts as a measurement rule only, so a false drop here cannot affect a review.
